Starlink is becoming a GAME CHANGER for airlines, driving higher customer satisfaction, stronger loyalty and even influencing which airline passengers choose to fly with

And the numbers are absolutely extraordinary:

• United Airlines — Customers are choosing United specifically because of Starlink, with the airline seeing opportunities to turn them into long-term loyal passengers

• Alaska/Hawaiian — Guest satisfaction is 20% higher on Starlink-equipped flights, while nearly 75% of non-members using the onboard portal signed up for Atmos Rewards

• Virgin Atlantic — Onboard connectivity satisfaction has increased by more than 40 points, with Starlink also helping attract new Flying Club members

• airBaltic — Net Promoter Scores are approximately 9 points higher on Starlink-equipped flights

• ZIPAIR — Passenger revenue grew 12.3% YoY, with JAL highlighting fleetwide Starlink connectivity alongside flexible pricing

Starlink has become a real competitive advantage, improving the passenger experience, strengthening customer loyalty, and giving people another reason to choose which airline they fly with

The future of in-flight connectivity is becoming a major part of how airlines compete

quoted_tweet.author: Yun-Ta Tsai
quoted_tweet.text:
In Ian Banks' Culture books, the Culture is a civilization of compute abundance. Each General System Vehicle is a loose sandbox environment practicing different ideologies, and citizens freely move between ships to experience different lifestyles.

Want communal life? There's a ship. Ultra-orthodox religion? Another. Beach chilling? One famous for its beaches.

With enormous compute, you don't need to trade off who decides the trajectories. Just launch another docker station for another rollout. In that world, your autonomy is backed by the compute.
